item.title: Wyoming - Wikipedia
item.description: Wyoming (/ waɪˈoʊmɪŋ / ⓘ wy-OH-ming) [7] is a landlocked state in the Mountain West subregion of the Western United States. It borders Montana to the north and northwest, South Dakota and Nebraska to the east, Idaho to the west, Utah to the southwest, and Colorado to the south.

item.description: Learn how to best experience Wyoming's national parks, where to spot wildlife, how to find the perfect dude ranch and more. Order your free Wyoming Travelers Journal and explore Wyoming maps and itineraries to plan the perfect vacation.

item.title: State of Wyoming - About Wyoming
item.description: Wyoming is home to the world’s first national park and the country’s first national forest. These and other public lands, along with millions of acres of privately-owned land provide a diverse landscape for more than 800 species of fish and wildlife.

item.title: Wyoming | Capital, Map, Population, History, Geography, & Facts ...
item.description: Wyoming, constituent state of the United States of America. Wyoming became the 44th state of the union on July 10, 1890. It ranks 10th among the 50 U.S. states in terms of total area.

item.title: 21 Things Wyoming Is Known And Famous For - Nomads Unveiled
item.description: Wyoming is significant for its breathtaking natural wonders, conservation efforts, energy production, and rich cowboy culture. The state is home to iconic destinations such as Yellowstone National Park and Grand Teton National Park.

item.title: Wyoming Maps & Facts - World Atlas
item.description: Wyoming is a western US state that shares its northern border with Montana, its eastern border with South Dakota and Nebraska, its southern border with Colorado and Utah, and its western border with Idaho.

item.description: Relive the spirit of the frontier at rodeos, cattle drives, dude ranches and history museums. item.title: Cheyenne, Wyoming - Wikipedia
item.description: Cheyenne is situated on Crow Creek and Dry Creek. It is the county seat of Laramie County. Cheyenne was established within the Dakota Territory in 1867 as a junction along the Union Pacific Railroad. Local residents named the town for the Cheyenne people.
